regression_determination.verdict: NOT a regression from S57 or S58. It is a long-standing gap in the default security callback, first reachable in this consumer once S60 repaired the workload.
evidence: ssl_get_min_max_version (src/ssl/statem/statem_lib.rs) and ssl_security_default_callback (src/ssl/ssl_lib.rs) are byte-identical at pre-S58 commit 90107ceda and at HEAD aa7a66583 (SHA-256 of the extracted function bodies match: min/max 88cc1b322e2ffd5b..., callback 5d1b5554859da53b...).
git blame places the version-selection block and its two SSL_R_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL fatals in ce686ee36 (2026-10-04), and the default callback in 0da2ee0ea (2026-10-03); both predate S57 and S58.

S57 (4304cccb9) touches only src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs; S58 (7bdc53d83) changes peer/shared sigalg ownership and does not touch the callback or the version walk. The S58 sigalg path is exercised by the same reproduction with SSL_OP_NO_TLSv1 removed and completes on the pre-fix candidate, so S58's changes are not implicated.
The authority has the same version-option configuration and succeeds, so the consumer's configuration is valid.

root_cause: ssl_security_default_callback answered 1 for every operation, so ssl_method_error's SSL_SECOP_VERSION check never enforced the security level's TLS1.2 floor; with SSL_OP_NO_TLSv1 opening a hole in the version table, ssl_get_min_max_version selected SSLv3 as the maximum and commit_client_hello rejected every ClientHello as SSL_R_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL.

mechanism.authority_rule: ssl/ssl_cert.c:1285-1297 (ssl_security_default_callback): non-DTLS versions <= TLS1_1_VERSION are refused at level > 0; DTLS versions below DTLS1.2 are refused at level > 0; a context-only VERSION query answers 0. OpenSSL's default level is 2 (include/openssl/tls1.h OPENSSL_TLS_SECURITY_LEVEL), matching the crate's cert_new.
mechanism.walk: ssl/statem/statem_lib.c:2481-2576 (ssl_get_min_max_version) treats an enabled method below a hole as the new selected version. With the permissive callback, TLS1.1 and SSLv3 were 'enabled' below the SSL_OP_NO_TLSv1 hole, so the final selected version was SSLv3 and max_version became SSLv3.
mechanism.consumer_path: charybdis sets SSL_OP_NO_TLSv1 on a version-flexible TLS_method() context, which is exactly the hole this needs; S60 made the workload reach the TLS listener, so the resulting SSLV3_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE became observable.

files.change: Implemented ssl_get_security_level_bits (level clamp 0..5 and the authority's minbits table) and the full SSL_SECOP_VERSION arm of ssl_security_default_callback, including the DTLS ordering and the authority's 0 answer for a context-only VERSION query. Also modelled the authority's level-0 SSL_SECOP_TMP_DH <80-bit refusal. The other operations keep the permissive answer S58 recorded as a residual; their level checks would change cipher and sigalg availability and are a separate boundary, so they were deliberately not widened or narrowed here.
